text.p: Jake's Pizza International Inc said Monday its board of directors resigned effective July 22, 1997 because the company could not obtain adequate directors and officers liability insurance coverage due to its financial difficulties.

Directors resigned when John Flowers, the company's president, chief executive officer and chairman, informed them of the company's inability to retain adequate directors and officers insurance, Jake's Pizza said in a news release.
The board, however, was not in disagreement with the direction of the company under Flowers' leadership or his performance when they tendered their resignations, it said.
"This is a difficult time for the company and all of our franchises. We continue to reduce our costs at the company level and support the franchisees," Flowers said.
Jake's Pizza operates restaurants in Illinois, Arizona, Florida, Indiana, North Carolina and Missouri.
The company reported a net loss for its fiscal 1997 first quarter ended December 31, 1996 of $186,266 or $0.16 a share on revenues of $226,781 reflecting costs of reorganizing the company.
Company officials were not immediately available to provide more details. ((Chicago newsdesk 312 408 8787))
